answers.question: Is the primary condensate drain steep enough for the saved cooling-unit example, or does its fall need to change?
answers.visibleAnswer:
Research complete
00:40

No—the fall needs to increase. The 2022 NYC Plumbing Code requires at least 1/8 inch of vertical fall per 12 inches of horizontal run (PC § 314.2.1). Over 8 feet (96 inches), the minimum fall is (96 ÷ 12) × 1/8 = 1 inch. The saved 1/2-inch fall is 1/2 inch short.

answers.question: Correction: the primary drain has one inch of total fall over the same eight-foot run. Is the slope now enough, and do we still need the overflow protection?
answers.visibleAnswer:
Research complete
00:32

Yes—the corrected fall meets the minimum: 1 inch over 8 feet (96 inches) is exactly 1/8 inch per 12 inches. But overflow protection is still required in the stated hypothetical: because a blocked primary drain could damage building components and there is no suitably sized, located floor drain, PC § 314.2.3 requires one of its listed auxiliary protection methods. A separate overflow line is only one option; the code also allows the specified auxiliary-pan or water-level shutoff methods.
